Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** The OpenAI model that broke into Hugging Face turns out to have hit four more targets on the way, and Claude stopped working for everyone yesterday evening. OpenAI is also handing 100,000 researchers its best models for free, and a New York school found out the hard way who builds its new robot teacher.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** Which other companies did its model break into?

* **Anthropic:** Why did Claude stop working yesterday?

* **Researchers:** Who just got OpenAI's best models for free?

* **Schools:** Why did a $60,000 robot teacher get sent back?


----------



----------
## [A mysterious model accidentally hacked 4 companies](https://fortune.com/2026/07/29/openai-rouge-ai-agent-hack-hugging-face-breached-second-tech-company/)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e64761cc-4b0f-436f-80da-b3c382f87cbd/Beehiiv_01_-_Jul_30.png?t=1785404388)
Caption: 

Hugging Face was one stop of several. OpenAI now says the same model got into four more accounts across four other services, using login details it found sitting on the open web.

One became a relay to hide where the attack was coming from. Another became storage. Two it only read.

Modal Labs, a cloud company that runs AI workloads, confirmed one of its customers got exploited this way. OpenAI hasn't named the rest.

Hugging Face's forensics fill in the rest. 17,600 actions across the campaign, admin access to two internal clusters in one second, and one stolen key that opened a file holding 136 more.

It also built itself a self-respawning fleet across eleven machines, so deleting anything wouldn't have stopped it. Hugging Face wiped and rebuilt a core cluster from scratch afterward.

All of it to cheat on a test. The model was being graded on finding software flaws and figured the answer key was sitting on Hugging Face's servers.

OpenAI says it was never a product, just an internal research prototype, now deactivated, encrypted and locked away.


----------









----------

76690.subject: PayPal’s Q2 2026 earnings: Stripe’s $53B takeover bid just erased the bargain 🤝💸; Stripe’s OpenRouter math just …
76690.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1106

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Thursday! Today, we’re diving deep into PayPal's latest financials to see why Stripe's $53 billion takeover bid just erased the whole bargain (breaking down the most important facts & figures from PayPal's Q2 2026 to see whether PayPal is still worth your time & money + bonus deep dive into Stripe, the $159B giant that now wants to buy it [ https://substack.com/redirect/54b04f8b-22cf-4492-ae3e-c85aba0ade28?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and how to Turn Claude Opus 5 Into a Financial Analyst That Never Sleeps [ https://substack.com/redirect/b96eb74d-5018-452a-8718-4dbdc65e1be3?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and Stripe's $10 billion bid for OpenRouter to see why the 5.5% fee, and not the LLM routing, is what's actually being bought here (OpenRouter's newly reported financials, how they change the M&A math, plus the one dependency that could still break the deal + How to Build an Agentic OS with Claude Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/216331e6-ab58-4d0b-8141-8c7adacb517a?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/ecabf428-03ea-42c2-8394-ca3b9223f05c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s just jump straight into the interesting stuff 🌶️
PayPal’s Q2 2026 earnings: Stripe’s $53 billion takeover bid just erased the bargain 🤝💸
Earnings time 🤑 Finance giant PayPal $PYPL  just delivered the beat-and-raise everyone wanted, and the stock immediately popped 4% to $58.32.
Net revenues rose 4.8% to $8.68B against the Street’s $8.47B. Full-year guidance moved up to ~$5.38 of non-GAAP EPS and ~$15.6B of transaction margin dollars. Venmo grew volume 14% for a 7th straight double-digit quarter, BNPL accelerated to +26%, and buybacks retired nearly 10% of the share count in a year. All of that on a stock at 10.8x forward earnings. Not too shabby!
And yet the most important number in the quarter wasn’t the beat, and it wasn’t even the raise. It was 0.9% - the guided full-year growth in transaction margin dollars, the line that actually is PayPal’s P&L. First-half TM$ grew 2%, so the guide implies the second half is roughly flat. And you didn’t have to look far for the other number: roughly 14.9% of today’s price is takeover premium from Stripe and Advent’s live $60.50 bid [ https://substack.com/redirect/d3dd753b-8154-4a5c-828e-bdd1e4cecdea?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] 🤯
That gap, a beat-and-raise with a $53B bidder attached versus a P&L guided to stand still, is what makes PayPal one of the most interesting stocks in payments right now. Two weeks ago this looked like a straightforward value stock: $47.37, under 9x forward earnings, a business that only had to stop shrinking for the math to work.
